e1_title: XGBoost is the most accurate and fast
e1: All three exceed 99.8% accuracy, so accuracy hides the difference; macro F1 does not. XGBoost was chosen on cross-validation (the highest). On the test run it ties with the MLP (paired bootstrap) and beats Random Forest; on three extra unseen wards it is best 3 times out of 3.
e1_notes: Selection used cross-validation only. The 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of the macro-F1 difference is 0.004 to 0.031 against Random Forest (a real lead) and 0.000 to 0.018 against the MLP (a tie). On the extra wards XGBoost averages 0.993, the MLP 0.982 and Random Forest 0.979. XGBoost trains in 32 s and needs 2.28 ms per flow; Random Forest is 11x slower per flow and weaker on spoofing.
confusion: Random Forest calls 10% of impostor spoofing flows normal; XGBoost and the MLP catch 98% and 99%. The evidence is a few weak twin signals that bagging outvotes and boosting focuses on.
confusion_notes: Rows are true classes, columns predictions, normalised per row. Loud attacks are easy for all models. The impostor publishes under a victim's identity; only sequence numbers, the cross-sensor residual and the sender's registry status give it away.
ablation: Adding the 11 twin features lifts XGBoost from 0.835 to 0.981 and spoofing recall from 28% to 97%. Raw vitals alone add little: consistency is what matters.
ablation_notes: Biometric features alone are nearly useless because the fake vitals are plausible. Network plus biometric, the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 design, is no better than network alone here. The twin features (sequence integrity, monitor versus wearable residual, registry checks) make the difference. Twin features are 20% of the inputs but carry about a quarter of the SHAP attribution.
zero_day: Trained without one family, supervised recall on it averages only 0.33 (XGBoost). The Isolation Forest reaches 0.72: strong on DoS, scans and exfiltration, weak on spoofing (0.17) and data alteration (0.30). Adding the twin rules closes that gap: all three layers together reach 0.97.
zero_day_notes: Each row is a detector, each column an attack family that was removed from training. The hybrid of XGBoost and the Isolation Forest reaches 0.73 at 1.20% FPR; adding the twin rules gives 0.97 at 1.50%. The next slide explains the rules.
rules_notes: The rules need no attack labels: each threshold is the 99.9th percentile of its signal in normal training traffic. They are strongest exactly where the learners are weakest, on unseen spoofing (0.99) and data alteration (0.89). The cost is more false alerts: in the live run 36 became 91, so the rules are an option (--twin-rules). At the 99.99th percentile their false positive rate falls to 0.12% but unseen-spoofing recall falls to 0.84.
sensitivity: Low-intensity data alteration is the hardest case (XGBoost recall 0.90). Shorter windows detect sooner: mean time-to-detect 10.1 s at 10 s, 7.0 s at 5 s and 5.3 s at 2 s, with macro F1 0.980, 0.981 and 0.960. We keep 5 s.
sensitivity_notes: The test run contains no high-intensity spoofing or unauthorised-access campaign, so those bars are missing. Exfiltration raises the mean delay because it is only visible once the upload starts.
realtime_notes: Replay of the test run: 30/30 campaigns, median 3.7 s. New live twin: 12/12, median 3.5 s. 4,782 alerts collapse into 34 incidents. Most 'false' alerts are the Isolation Forest, nurse pump pauses, or the healthy wearable of a patient whose monitor is spoofed, which still points at the right bed.
limitations: Simulated data: real devices and attackers vary more, so absolute scores are optimistic
Twin rules catch unseen integrity attacks but add false alerts
Nurse pump commands, including restores after an attack, can look like rogue commands
Flow labels can disagree with bed-level reality
WUSTL-EHMS-2020 benchmark script ready but not yet run
future: Validate on real captures and WUSTL-EHMS-2020
Calibrate twin rules per device to cut false alerts
Feed command source and clinical orders into pump features
Clinician-approved automatic isolation of high-risk devices
conclusion: RQ1: the ward twin generates exactly labelled, controllable IoMT data
RQ2: XGBoost gives the best balance (macro F1 0.981, 2.28 ms per flow)
RQ3: twin features lift spoofing recall from 28% to 97%
RQ4: Isolation Forest plus twin rules lift unseen-attack recall from 0.33 to 0.97
RQ5: all 30 test campaigns detected in real time, median 3.7 s
